    • ABSOLUTE_ERROR

      private static final double ABSOLUTE_ERROR
      Maximum allowed difference between the estimator and the in-test reference implementation (a direct transcription of Groves' Kinematics_ECI.m using matrix operations). Both perform the same arithmetic and only differ in the order of a few floating point operations, hence only rounding errors remain: ECI velocities are of the order of 1e2 m/s, so their rounding error (about 1e-14 m/s) divided by the shortest time interval (0.02 s) is of the order of 1e-12 m/s^2. This value passes for both passes (small and large) of the SEEDED_RUNS seeded runs of the estimation tests, which were observed to keep passing when this value is reduced down to 1e-13, so no larger value is needed.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • ROUND_TRIP_ABSOLUTE_ERROR

      private static final double ROUND_TRIP_ABSOLUTE_ERROR
      Maximum allowed difference between the kinematics fed to ECIInertialNavigator and the kinematics recovered by ECIKinematicsEstimator from the navigated frame. Estimator and navigator are exact inverses of each other when gravitation is evaluated at the position at the start of the time interval, hence only rounding errors remain: velocities are of the order of 1e2 m/s (they include Earth rotation), so that their rounding error (about 1e-14 m/s) divided by the shortest time interval (0.1 s) stays several orders of magnitude below this value (the round trip was observed to keep passing when this value is reduced down to 1e-12). Any deviation from the reference algorithm is orders of magnitude larger (1e-6 m/s^2 or more).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • MIN_POSITION_SPECIFIC_FORCE_DIFFERENCE

      private static final double MIN_POSITION_SPECIFIC_FORCE_DIFFERENCE
      Minimum specific force difference, expressed in meters per squared second (m/s^2), that must exist between kinematics estimated with gravitation evaluated at the old position and at the new position for the long round trip time interval. In that interval the body moves several hundred meters with respect to the ECI frame (because of Earth rotation), and gravitation gradient is about 1.5e-6 s^-2, so the actual difference is of the order of 1e-4 m/s^2, well above this value and well above ROUND_TRIP_ABSOLUTE_ERROR.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • testEstimate

      @Test void testEstimate() throws com.irurueta.navigation.frames.InvalidSourceAndDestinationFrameTypeException, com.irurueta.geometry.InvalidRotationMatrixException
      Checks that all ECIKinematicsEstimator.estimate(double, com.irurueta.navigation.frames.CoordinateTransformation, com.irurueta.navigation.frames.CoordinateTransformation, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, com.irurueta.navigation.inertial.BodyKinematics) overloads are consistent: overloads receiving an explicit position or the previous frame evaluate gravitation at the provided or previous position, and overloads receiving only the current frame evaluate gravitation at the current position. Each seeded run executes a small pass (short time interval, small attitude variation) and a large pass (long time interval, large attitude variation).
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.frames.InvalidSourceAndDestinationFrameTypeException - never happens.
      com.irurueta.geometry.InvalidRotationMatrixException - never happens.
